chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Buffalo and the union problem (second version)
summary: Peanuts is picked up in Buffalo; the Royals and union trouble; the owner is Altman.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: You didn't have any trouble with the band until you got burned out, and the Plantation.
You stayed around--when did you first go to Buffalo, up around there?
This is what I do wrong, when I get started--
Lay down, partner; lay down.
You played in Cincinatti with the same bunch of guys; no changes; you couldn't get Peanuts.
That's right.
You got Peanuts upstate, in Buffalo; didn't you? I'm pretty sure you got him in Buffalo.
You played the Paradise?
No, (inaudible) Royals.
That's where you played in Buffalo.
That was some place.
That's where you got in trouble with the union; right?
We had a little problem.
You didn't know what the scale was, but you were playing for under scale or something like that? Without being aware of it.
We didn't know it. I think it was really a frameup.
It must have been, because you did very well up there.
We did very fine. We booked the place up.
That's the guy who became famous up there in Buffalo?
Yeah; Altman? That's the guy we worked for.
So you were there about two months?
We were there quite a few months.
